title: NFL Catchup: A Big Extension In Dallas, And What Is Aaron Rodgers Doing In Practice?
description:
Monday featured a major contract agreement for Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and an extension for New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry.
Aaron Rodgers also did something relatively unusual at Pittsburgh Steelers practice, while there's another update to share on Aaron Donald's potential return to play.
Star defensive lineman Quinnen Williams has agreed to a three-year, $105.9 million extension with the Cowboys, NFL Network reported Monday.
The New England Patriots agreed to terms on a two-year contract extension with tight end Hunter Henry on Monday, ESPN reported Monday.
Quarterback Aaron Rodgers took an unconventional turn during practice on Monday, lining up as an edge defender against his team's second-string offense.
text:
Preseason officially kicks off for 30 of 32 teams across the NFL this week, but contract matters continue to dominate the news.

Monday featured a major contract agreement for Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams and an extension for New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry. Aaron Rodgers also did something relatively unusual at Pittsburgh Steelers practice, while there's another update to share on Aaron Donald's potential return to play.

Here is the latest news from around the league.

Star defensive lineman Quinnen Williams has agreed to a three-year, $105.9 million extension with the Cowboys, NFL Network reported Monday. The deal for Williams reportedly includes $101 million guaranteed with $63.35 million due at signing.

Williams is entering year two in Dallas after arriving at last year’s trade deadline. With a wave of massive contracts hitting the defensive line market this summer, all eyes now shift to the ripple effect on the rest of the league.

"Usually, if you have two people wanting to get something done, it can get done. ... Every deal is different," Cowboys Executive Vice President Stephen Jones told reporters, via The Athletic. "You just hit certain bumps in the road where things don't. It's not because we don't want to. ... We're always in the mode if it's the right situation to do a deal."

Next in line for a payday at defensive tackle is Tampa Bay Buccaneers standout Vita Vea, who requested a trade at the start of training camp. Maybe a new contract for Williams could reignite negotiations between Vea and the Buccaneers? Vea is entering the final year of his contract, which holds a $17 million base salary.

The Cowboys put quite the investment into Williams before the extension. At last year’s trade deadline, they traded defensive lineman Mazi Smith, a 2026 second-round pick and the more favorable of their two 2027 first-round picks for Williams.

The New England Patriots agreed to terms on a two-year contract extension with tight end Hunter Henry on Monday, ESPN reported Monday. The extension reportedly carries a base value of $16 million with incentives that could raise the total value to $20 million, including $14.5 million guaranteed.

The 31-year-old tight end had one year remaining on his previous contract and is now locked in through the 2027 season. Henry served as a primary target for quarterback Drake Maye last season, hauling in 60 receptions for 768 yards and a team-high seven touchdowns.

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers took an unconventional turn during practice on Monday, lining up as an edge defender against his team's second-string offense.

Video captured the veteran quarterback working on defensive reps during team drills. The moment offered a lighthearted break during competitive practice sessions as Rodgers continues his training camp workload.

As the 42-year-old Rodgers returned to the Pittsburgh Steelers for one more season, the quarterback made news over the weekend when he credited Mike Tomlin for helping him get his spark back last year.

"I’m thankful for last year with Coach Tomlin, because he helped me get that love back, that deep love back for the game," Rodgers told SiriusXM Radio. "That, you know, tearing my Achilles and going through a year of rehab, and just never feeling like myself, it just kind of beats you up a little bit, and I didn’t want that to be my ending in the game that I love so much, and Mike and being around the guys, got me that love back, and I was content in walking away."

While Tomlin left the Steelers this offseason, Rodgers nearly followed him until the team decided to hire one of his former coaches with the Green Bay Packers, Mike McCarthy, to replace him.

"They hired Mike McCarthy, and I was like, ‘OK, maybe we need a full circle here, me and Mike need a full circle here,'" Rodgers said.

Aaron Donald is continuing to spark rumors of his return. His trainer shared a video of Donald training alongside Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Braden Fiske.

The video came a few days after Donald had an official workout with the Rams, only heightening the speculation that he'll return. It's been rumored that his decision could come soon, with Rams head coach Sean McVay saying in late July that Donald would likely make a decision later in August.

Donald, a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and eight-time First-Team All-Pro selection, has maintained an active training regimen following his retirement from professional football in 2024.

title: Fantasy football injury updates for Patrick Mahomes, Malik Nabers, more - The Huddle
description:
The 2026 NFL season is around the corner and fantasy football managers will soon be gearing up for their drafts.
As they prepare their fantasy football rankings and cheat sheets for the big day, managers will need to keep a keen eye on injuries.
Numerous notable players around the league are dealing with injuries that could impact their availability for the beginning of the 2026 NFL season.
Will players like Patrick Mahomes, Malik Nabers and George Kittle be able to get on the field in Week 1?
Here are the latest injury updates for top fantasy football producers as the 2026 NFL season draws nearer.
text:
The 2026 NFL season is around the corner and fantasy football managers will soon be gearing up for their drafts.

As they prepare their fantasy football rankings and cheat sheets for the big day, managers will need to keep a keen eye on injuries.

Numerous notable players around the league are dealing with injuries that could impact their availability for the beginning of the 2026 NFL season. Many of them are recovering from maladies suffered the previous season but a handful have been dinged up during the early stages of training camp.

Will players like Patrick Mahomes, Malik Nabers and George Kittle be able to get on the field in Week 1? Here are the latest injury updates for top fantasy football producers as the 2026 NFL season draws nearer.

Fantasy football injury updates

QB Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs

Chiefs coach Andy Reid hasn't committed to Mahomes playing in the preseason, but Mahomes has noted his injured knee "feels great" as he continues to target a return to the field by Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

Given that Mahomes hasn't been categorically ruled out of the preseason, it looks like the soon-to-be 31-year-old has a good chance to be on the field in Week 1. The bigger question is whether he will be a QB1 in fantasy football or whether the Chiefs will lean more on free agent addition Kenneth Walker III early in the season as Mahomes continues to recover from the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

QB Michael Penix Jr., Atlanta Falcons

Penix entered Falcons training camp still working toward full medical clearance as he recovers from a torn ACL he suffered midway through the 2025 campaign. Even if he can return to the field during training camp and the preseason, he doesn't project to be much of a fantasy asset. He averaged just one touchdown pass per game last season and is no guarantee to beat Tua Tagovailoa for the starting job in Atlanta.

RB Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks

Charbonnet is recovering from a torn ACL he suffered during the Seahawks' playoff win over the 49ers. Mike Macdonald hasn't provided a concrete timeline on his return to action and it remains unclear whether he will be on the field in Week 1.

Once healthy, Charbonnet figures to split carries with Seattle's first-round rookie, Jadarian Price. Price's presence coupled with Charbonnet's injury makes the fourth-year veteran hard to trust as anything more than a low-end flex or top handcuff.

RB Isiah Pacheco, Detroit Lions

Pacheco is dealing with a sprained MCL he suffered during Detroit's training camp. The good news is that Lions coach Dan Campbell said he "feels pretty good" about the prospect of Pacheco being ready for the start of the season.

Pacheco signed with the Lions in free agency to help replace David Montgomery as the foil to Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs is expected to get a lion's share of his team's work at running back, but Pacheco still makes for a good handcuff and potential touchdown-based flex option.

WR Malik Nabers, New York Giants

Nabers' status for Week 1 has long been murky as he has attempted to recover from a torn ACL he suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 NFL season. The 23-year-old avoided the physically unable to perform (PUP) list entering training camp and appears to be on track to play in Week 1 against the Cowboys, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan.

Nabers is expected to be the Giants' No. 1 receiver and should quickly become a favorite target of Jaxson Dart. The LSU product has averaged 77.6 receiving yards across 19 NFL games to date, giving him true WR1 upside in fantasy football.

WR Mike Evans, San Francisco 49ers

Evans has been nursing a quad injury during the early stages of his first training camp with the 49ers. Kyle Shanahan said the team is just "being smart" with the soon-to-be 33-year-old and that the 49ers expect him back on the field to start the season.

Evans is set to be San Francisco's No. 1 receiver in 2026, provided he can stay on the field. The former Buccaneers saw a streak of 11 consecutive 1,000-yard seasons come to an end in 2025 because of hamstring and clavicle injuries. If healthy, Evans should still have the volume needed to be a solid WR2 in fantasy football formats in 2026.

WR Luther Burden III, Chicago Bears

Burden suffered a groin injury at Chicago's practice on Aug. 8. He is set to miss the preseason because of the malady, but the team is hoping he will be healthy for Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season.

Burden had been a hot commodity in fantasy circles before his injury. While he remains a breakout candidate, his injury should cement his status as Chicago's No. 2 receiver behind Rome Odunze, who should be selected ahead of his younger counterpart in fantasy drafts.

WR Alec Pierce, Indianapolis Colts

Pierce has been sidelined for all of Colts camp to date while recovering from offseason ankle surgery. Coach Shane Steichen has yet to provide a timeline for the receiver, who signed a $114 million extension this offseason, to return, simply saying he only wants Pierce back "whenever he's 100%."

Pierce is expected to be the Colts' No. 1 receiver in 2026. His deep-play capabilities – he led the NFL with 21.3 yards per reception in 2025 – will make him a boom-or-bust WR2 in fantasy formats. If he misses any time, Josh Downs would move to the top of Indy's wide receiver depth chart, though Downs is currently dealing with a minor groin issue of his own.

TE George Kittle, San Francisco 49ers

Kittle was placed on the PUP list by the 49ers to open training camp as he recovers from a torn Achilles he suffered during the 2025 NFL playoffs. The 32-year-old has expressed a desire to play the team's Week 1 game in Melbourne against the Rams, but there's no guarantee he will be able to come off the PUP list before then.

As long as Kittle remains sidelined, Jake Tonges and Luke Farrell will split time at tight end. Tonges would be the bigger fantasy factor as a receiver while Farrell is more known for his blocking prowess.

TE Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers

Kraft suffered a torn ACL midway through the 2025 season. He was originally on the PUP list to start training camp but was activated July 31 and returned to the practice field recently in the hopes of ramping up to play in Week 1.

Kraft averaged an impressive 61.1 yards per game and 15.3 yards per reception last season. That should help make him a top-five fantasy tight end in 2026 if he is able to return to the field at full strength in Week 1.

TE Kenyon Sadiq, New York Jets

Sadiq recently endured a setback with a hernia surgery he had in May, but Jets coach Aaron Glenn expressed he is "very confident" the No. 16 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will be back on the field for Week 1.

Sadiq is expected to be the Jets' starting tight end in 2026 and is viewed as a sleeper option in fantasy circles thanks to his elite athleticism.

text:
ALLEN PARK, Mich. (AP) — Center Cade May, who was signed to anchor the Detroit Lions’ reworked offensive line, will be out for significant time because of a wrist injury, coach Dan Campbell said Monday.

“You hate it, I hate it for him because I felt like he was having a good camp and he’d grown so much in our system just since spring,” Campbell said.

He would not give a timeline on May’s return from what he described as a freak injury that happened at camp Sunday.

“It stinks, but I know he’ll work his way back and be ready to go at some point,” quarterback Jared Goff said.

May’s absence will give Seth McLaughlin and Juice Scruggs the opportunity to compete for the start at center. Scruggs was sidelined with a soft tissue injury on Monday, so McLaughlin got all the snaps with the starters while Michael Niese worked with the No. 2s.

Goff said communication was good with McLaughlin even though he had never had a snap from him before Monday.

“That’s the best way to find out on some of these guys, that’s all you can ask for. Man, it’s your shot, we’ll see where we can go with it,” Campbell said.

McLaughlin will start in the Lions’ preseason game at Cincinnati on Thursday.

“It’s the hand you’re dealt and you move on,’’ Campbell said.

Lions sign backup QB Josh Dobbs

Veteran Josh Dobbs was signed to replace quarterback Teddy Bridgewater, whose retirement was announced Sunday. It’s the second stint in Detroit for Dobbs, who spent two weeks on the practice squad in 2022.

“We really liked him and then he got poached, that’s kind of where it went,” Campbell said. “It’s good to get him back.”

Dobbs was on the field for Monday’s practice but did not take any reps. Rookie QB Luke Altmyer will start Thursday night. If Dobbs is up to speed, he could see action.

A fourth-round draft pick out of Tennessee by the Steelers in 2017, Dobbs has made 27 career appearances and 15 starts. He spent last season with the Patriots as Drake Maye’s backup. He appeared in four games and completed 7 of 10 passes for 65 yards.
